newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks close lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks close lower in thin trade.

text.p: Chilean shares closed broadly lower amid low turnover which reflected the lack of foreign buyers due to the U.S. Columbus Day holiday, said dealers.

The market is seen opening higher with the rally continuing for the rest of the week, provided U.S. long-term interest rates remain stable, said Pedro Santa Maria, finance manager of brokerage Socimer.
"The key factor is whether U.S. interest rates remain low. If they do, then investors will have to look for other alternatives including Latin American stocks," said Santa Maria.
The weighted IPSA index ended unofficially down 0.28 percent at 101.97 points.
The general IGPA index shed 0.16 percent to 5,545.43 points.
Volume was just five billion pesos - less than a half of the bolsa's usual trading turnover.
The low turnover reflected the token trade on Wall Street as a result of the holiday, they said.
Traders said they expect demand for Latin American American Depositary Receipts to be positive when Wall Street resumes more usual trading Tuesday.
Investors are starting to look to third quarter results which are starting to filter into the market and must officially be published by month-end, they said.
Companies expected to report good earnings include sugar-maker Iansa and fertilizer producer Soquimich, said dealers.
Losers included forestry firm Masisa, down 3.87 percent at 211 pesos, pension fund manager Provida, down 3.16 percent at 9,200 pesos and paper-maker CMPC which fell 2.01 percent at 5,370 pesos.
Winners included telecoms company Telex, up 2.7 percent at 1,330 pesos, copper products maker Madeco, up 0.93 percent at 980 pesos and winery Concha y Toro which rose 0.62 percent at 162 pesos.
